eyebrow: A tag is metadata, nothing more
caption: A key, with a constrained set of allowed values — an unlisted value is rejected at apply time.
A manually authored, custom tag — the most common case.

code:
ALTER TABLE raw_customer.customer_loyalty
MODIFY COLUMN
  first_name SET TAG tags.tasty_pii = 'NAME',
  phone_number SET TAG tags.tasty_pii = 'PHONE_NUMBER';
caption: Same tag key, a different value per column — recording what kind of PII it holds.

code:
SELECT
  tag_database,
  tag_schema,
  tag_name,
  column_name,
  tag_value
FROM TABLE(information_schema.tag_references_all_columns
  ('tb_101.raw_customer.customer_loyalty','table'));

-- also: SHOW TAGS IN SCHEMA tags;
-- tags also apply beyond columns:
-- ALTER DATABASE / SCHEMA / WAREHOUSE ... SET TAG
caption: One query pattern works no matter who — or what — applied the tag.
Snowflake's own system tag, applied automatically by data classification — no CREATE TAG statement behind this one.
A tag applied by a custom classifier's own regex logic — same querying pattern confirms it.
